title: Grateful Dead Live at The Ark on 1969-04-22
source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Reel -> Dat -> CD D

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a stellar 1969 Ark show with an epic Mountains Of The Moon → Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence, despite minor tape‑flip glitches.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its high energy and the monumental second‑set suite – Mountains Of The Moon into a soaring Dark Star that segues into Saint Stephen and a blistering Eleven. Reviewers also highlight Dupree’s, Morning Dew, Good Morning Little Schoolgirl and a powerful Lovelight, noting Jerry Garcia’s “genius” guitar work and Phil Lesh’s tight bass. The soundboard source is generally clear but suffers from some degraded sections and tape‑flip dropouts that keep the recording from being pristine.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (10 out of 12) give five stars and extol the musical performance, especially the Dark Star/Eleven suite; recording issues are mentioned but only as minor degradations, leading to a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall clear soundboard capture, but several reviewers note degraded audio in spots and tape‑flip dropouts that cause brief glitches.

standout_songs: Mountains Of The Moon > Dark Star > Saint Stephen > The Eleven
show_quality.setlist_flow: An energetic first set builds momentum, leading into a second‑set that showcases extended improvisation and seamless transitions; the highlight is the long Dark Star/Eleven suite, making the show feel cohesive and thrilling from start to finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar receives abundant praise – soaring solos, massive analog feedback, and moments described as "genius" especially during Dark Star and the Mountains Of The Moon jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh is noted for strong bass work and vocal contributions, holding down the pocket particularly in The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir (Bobby) is mentioned as low in the mix on The Eleven but praised for staying solid in the pocket and adding vocal harmony.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig’s organ/harmonica presence is referenced, including a brief "pig rap" and overall supportive playing, though no specific virtuoso moments are highlighted.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann gets nods for powerful drum rolls around the 24‑25 minute mark of Dark Star, adding intensity to the jam.
